Computer Science
Staff
Subject leader: Mrs A. Yalley
Intent
Our mission is to equip students to be tech savvy, confident to operate hardware and software efficiently through our effective, organised delivery of the curriculum. Students offered Computer Science are encouraged to problem solve, present their knowledge of computer architecture, ethics covering IT eg cybersecurity, and also explore and understand current applications such as artificial intelligence.
The subject offers fun and challenging lessons with the aim to train students to create programs by applying good programming skills, implement creative models through a range of topics covered in the Computing curriculum. They should finally be prepared and poised to handle prospects in the Computing / IT field.

Drama
Staff
Subject Leader: Mrs R. Wells
Intent
Our aim is to ensure that the study of Drama enables our students to become self-confident individuals, collaborative team players, empathetic, considerate and well-rounded citizens. Drama is a set of skills that can be used in any aspect of everyday life and allow our students to feel empowered and confident in the ‘real’ world. Students will develop an understanding of society and a broad world view, gain skills that will allow them to express themselves by using their imagination and creativity. Through our learning, we coach self-discipline and effective self-management in a professional environment, alongside the idiosyncratic life lesson of reflecting on your personal strengths whilst reflecting on your areas for development. Students who chose to further their study past Key Stage 3, will gain knowledge of theatre history and important influential practitioners in Drama and Theatre.

Art and Photography
Staff
Subject leader: Mrs C. Reed
Intent
The Art curriculum focuses on creativity, skills, and knowledge to develop self-confidence in our students. They will be encouraged to question ideas and concepts, analyse artwork, and find links between artists’ work and the wider world, exploring the diversity of culture, context and technique.
Our curriculum allows students to work in a safe, supportive and encouraging environment where they feel comfortable with taking risks in their learning. Students will explore their own creativity while developing life skills such as problem-solving, idea generation, and conceptual thinking.

Geography
Staff
Subject leader: Mr J. Sempill
Intent
We aim to inspire awe and wonder in every student, in every lesson. Students will be hungry to know more about the planet and human influences on it in both the built and natural environment. Students are empowered with the skills to be reflective and discerning contemporary global citizens where they can justify their opinions about global issues. Fieldwork is integral to student understanding at a local, national and global scale. We aim to challenge stereotypes and misconceptions about topical issues.

Homework
Every 12 weeks students will receive a home learning grid. Every week students can pick an activity to complete and submit via Teams to their teacher, this could be photos, sound bites or even models. They must choose from each category so at the end of each cycle they can spell CIRCLE, it cannot all be from one or two columns. Once completed they will receive a stamp on their learning passport, each completed cycle can be exchanged for a certificate and at the end of the year if all 3 cycles are completed students will receive a History golden star badge. Please upload all work to the Teams assignment. This is an ongoing homework with the expectation one activity is completed each week.
Homework will be set on Seneca Learning (please see parent mail for details of how to support your child with this), in addition to homework which will mostly be research tasks or exam practice. Students should expect to receive at least 2 pieces of homework a week.
Students should expect to spend a minimum of 4 hours per week engaging in Geography work outside of lessons. This should include completing homework, revision, wider reading and research and completing exam practice. If students feel that they have completed all required work, they should refer to the '10 things to do when you have nothing to do' document below.

History
Staff
Subject leader: Mrs S. Hinks
Intent
Through the studying of History, students will investigate chronologically a broad period of History that focuses on both British, European and International History in order to understand their own sense of place and belonging. Students will develop a wider understanding of the world around them and how the present is very much shaped by the past, thus enabling them to critically analyse current affairs and Historical milestones. During their learning journey, Amersham School students will be equipped with the skills and moral conscience that not only underpins our school values and ethos but allows them to flourish in the wider world.

SEN
At Amersham School we believe that each student has individual and unique needs. However, some students require more support than others.
If these students are to achieve their full potential, we must recognise this and plan accordingly. We acknowledge that a significant proportion of students will have special educational needs at some time in their school career. Many of these students may require help throughout their time in school, whilst others may need a little extra support for a short period to help overcome more temporary needs.
Amersham School aims to provide all students with strategies for dealing with their needs in a supportive environment, and to give them meaningful access to the National Curriculum.
When students complete their education at Amersham School, they should feel ready to confidently tackle new challenges and become a successful and fulfilled member of society.
Amersham School offers a limited number of SEN tours for students with EHCPs. These take place once a month on a Thursday at 9.30am and are limited to three families per date. To organise a tour, please contact the school office who will be able to advise on availability.

Business Studies
Staff
Lead teacher: Mr C. Hall
Intent
The intent of Business and Enterprise is to facilitate high quality and engaging teaching and learning experiences, which link to aspirational career choices and help drive the future economy of our country. Excellence, enjoyment and maximising the potential of our students is a core focus of implementation, whilst using up-to-date case studies and current affairs to inspire and engage our learners.
Developing Foundational Knowledge: equip students with a comprehensive understanding of fundamental business concepts, theories, principles, and practices. Through engaging and interactive learning experiences, students will gain proficiency in areas such as marketing, finance, accounting, human resources, operations management, entrepreneurship, and business ethics.
Instilling Ethical Awareness and Social Responsibility: nurture ethical awareness and social responsibility among students. By exploring ethical dilemmas faced by businesses and examining the principles of corporate social responsibility, students will develop a strong ethical compass and an understanding of the importance of conducting business in an ethical and sustainable manner.
Business Studies provides students with a well-rounded education that not only imparts essential business knowledge and skills but also fosters critical thinking, ethical awareness, global perspective, and a lifelong passion for learning and innovation. Through this comprehensive curriculum, we aim to prepare students to excel as responsible and visionary leaders in the dynamic world of business.

Ethics
Staff
Lead teacher: Miss M. Stevens
Intent
Ethics is a carousel subject studied in Years 9 and 10 to equip students with knowledge and skills beyond school life. Through topics such as diversity, gender, healthy relationships, managing money, and debates surrounding the use of animal testing, euthanasia and abortion, students explore real world dilemmas. The Ethics curriculum explores a range of global, cultural and religious perspectives, exploring customs and beliefs across the world, in order to encourage our students to become global citizens.

Media Studies
Staff
Subject leader: Mr J. Renaud
Intent
Media studies is an interdisciplinary field that examines the creation, production, distribution, and consumption of media. It encompasses a wide range of topics, including:
The intent of media studies is to provide students with a critical understanding of the media so that they can become informed and engaged consumers of media. Media studies also helps students to develop their own media literacy skills, which are essential for navigating the complex and ever-changing media environment. Students also gain empathy and understanding for cultures, genders, and ethnicities by observing and analysing representation. Analysis of set products expands students' ability to interpret the everyday world with empathy and creativity.

Media studies is an important field of study because it helps us to understand the world around us. The media are a powerful force in society, and it is important to be able to critically analyse their messages. Media studies also provides us with the tools we need to create our own media content and to participate in the public sphere.

Absence Reporting
If your child is unwell we ask that you telephone or email the school on the first day of absence and on every subsequent day.
The number to call is 01494 789009
The email address is attendance@amershamschool.org
When your child returns to school, please send in a written note to Mrs Podbury, Attendance Officer.
If your child has been unwell with a contagious illness eg sickness or diarrhoea, please ensure that a full 24 hours has passed without being poorly before they come back to school.
If your child is unwell early in the morning, please keep them at home until they are fully recovered.
Download an Application Form for Student Leave of Absence HERE. Please note that in line with government policy, we do not authorise any absence during term term.
